channel.title: Cybersecurity News
channel.description: Notable but non-breaking cybersecurity news, one finding per item: short summary plus link to the original story.

item.title: PHP2Shell now confirmed exploited in the wild: honeypots log working shells via public PoC
item.description:
Perplexity researcher Adel Karimi reports confirmed remote code execution of the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618/-109619) against his honeypots, with 35 shells launched from two IP addresses on October 24 using a four-stage chain that closely matches a public proof-of-concept.

Expel's Marcus Hutchins called it the highest-quality confirmation of in-the-wild exploitation so far. Karimi cautions the honeypots used a favorable single-worker Apache mod_php setup, and no second-stage payload was seen. CISA has published a Sigma detection rule but has not yet added the flaws to KEV. Patch to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35.

Sources: SecurityWeek, BleepingComputer

item.title: Siemens, Schneider Electric, ABB and other industrial vendors confirm OT products affected by PHP2Shell
item.description:
Siemens, Schneider Electric, ABB, Rockwell Automation and Johnson Controls have published advisories on the PHP2Shell flaws, and several confirm some industrial and OT products are affected.

Schneider lists EcoStruxure Security Expert (fixed in 1.48.4.0), ProLeiT LINEoptimize and EcoStruxure Control Engineering, the last with mitigations only for now. Other vendors are still assessing exposure.

Sources: SecurityWeek

item.title: Gheist campaign uses stolen GitHub tokens to dump Actions secrets from 850+ accounts' repos
item.description:
Wiz reports an automated campaign, active since September 15, that uses stolen GitHub tokens to push ci-sync-* branches with workflows that print repository secrets into Actions logs, then downloads the logs and deletes the runs. Wiz recovered more than 13,500 planted branches from more than 850 compromised accounts, including private enterprise repositories.

GitHub's safeguard for suspicious runs blocked public-repo attempts but does not cover private repositories or GitHub Enterprise Server. Affected orgs should rotate every secret the repo could read and revoke the token that pushed the branch.

Sources: The Hacker News

item.title: Two CVSS 9.9 Wasmtime flaws let malicious WebAssembly modules escape the sandbox
item.description:
The Bytecode Alliance fixed two critical bugs in Wasmtime's Cranelift compiler (one ARM64-only, CVE-2026-115893) that let an attacker-supplied WebAssembly module escape its sandbox. Risk is highest for platforms that compile other people's modules, such as Fastly Compute.

No attacks are reported. Update to 36.0.19, 48.0.7, 49.0.4 or 50.0.0; unsupported lines, including 24.x LTS, get no fix.

Sources: The Hacker News

item.title: Fortinet ships fixes for critical AI-found FortiOS flaws, withholding details until November 10
item.description:
Fortinet released security hardening updates last week for FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator, fixing critical vulnerabilities found with AI models and validated by humans.

Details stay embargoed until November 10, 2026. CISO Carl Windsor warned that attackers can use AI to find and weaponize bugs, so admins should update now rather than wait for the disclosure.

Sources: Help Net Security

item.title: Microsoft ships out-of-band .NET updates for Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497
item.description:
Microsoft released out-of-band .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22 and 10.0.14 on October 25 to fix the Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write (CVE-2026-111497) behind the Node.js "Node2Shell" research, plus other fixes including a Blazor WebAssembly debugger RCE in .NET 10.

Apps are exposed only if they decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data; ASP.NET Core and HttpClient automatic decompression are off by default. Self-contained and NativeAOT apps must be rebuilt and redeployed.

Sources: .NET Blog, Microsoft advisory

item.title: Unpatched Tailscale SSH flaws let one compromised device reach root on other servers ("Tailworm")
item.description:
Researcher Erica Windisch of Cyberdione Labs published "Tailworm," showing that an attacker who already controls one device on a Tailscale network can use Tailscale SSH port forwarding to get root on other servers that the access rules let that device reach, with no stolen passwords or keys. The lab tests covered Tailscale 1.104.2 and headscale 0.29.5; on headscale, forwarding cannot be disabled, so every SSH grant should be treated as root on the target.

As of publication there is no Tailscale security bulletin, CVE, or fixed version. Tailscale says it is working on fixes and is not recommending everyone disable Tailscale SSH; hosted-service admins can turn off forwarding per rule.

Sources: The Hacker News, Tailworm report, Tailscale statement on Reddit

item.title: PHP2Shell: Palo Alto Networks and Trail of Bits report first confirmed compromises and post-exploit activity
item.description:
As of late Friday, Palo Alto Networks and Trail of Bits say there are now confirmed compromises and post-exploitation activity tied to PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), the unauthenticated PHP remote code execution flaws patched on October 21. Researchers say weaponizing the bugs is hard, which is why mass exploitation hasn't been seen yet, but many internet-facing PHP servers remain unpatched. Amazon has said exploitation began as early as October 17, before patches shipped.

Sources: TechCrunch, Unit 42

item.title: Eye Security pushed 2 million updates to disable abandoned Popcorn Time updater that could have fueled a botnet
item.description:
Dutch firm Eye Security found that the updater in Time4Popcorn, an abandoned Popcorn Time fork, kept calling an unregistered domain, so anyone who registered it could have pushed code to the machines still running it. The firm registered the domain itself, saw about 50 requests a second, and between November 2025 and March 2026 sent more than 2 million updates to switch the updater off. It presented the work, dubbed Operation IXIM, at Hack.lu on October 22.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: CISA adds exploited Collabora Online built-in CODE server command injection CVE-2026-110447 to KEV
item.description:
CISA added CVE-2026-110447, an unauthenticated OS command injection in the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server app for Nextcloud, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 23 with an October 26 deadline and forensic triage required. The bug in the app's proxy.php runs commands as the web server user, but only while the built-in CODE server isn't running, such as after a restart, upgrade or crash. Disabling the app isn't enough: upgrade it to 26.4.303 or later or remove it. Standalone Collabora Online servers aren't affected.

Sources: Nextcloud forum, Collabora advisory, CISA KEV

item.title: Kaspersky: APT41-linked BlackX UEFI bootkit bypasses Secure Boot on patched Windows PCs missing revocations
item.description:
Kaspersky says a new UEFI bootkit called BlackX, an updated BlackLotus, hit diplomatic organizations in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan in early 2026, and it suspects China-linked APT41. BlackX loads before Windows to undermine startup and third-party security defenses and keep long-term covert access. It works on fully patched systems where Microsoft's manual Secure Boot revocation mitigations were never applied, though attackers first need admin or physical access.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Ruby patches three Onigmo regex engine bugs behind four critical GitLab RCE flaws
item.description:
Ruby released 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 to fix three memory-corruption bugs in Onigmo, its built-in regular expression engine, which can lead to code execution when an app compiles a regex from attacker-controlled text. The bugs sit behind four critical GitLab CVEs patched between September 23 and October 21, including two from October (CVE-2026-97229 and CVE-2026-110264) that need no account. Regexp.timeout and pattern-length caps do not help, Ruby 4.0.8 misses one fix, and Ruby 3.2 and earlier get no patch. No in-the-wild exploitation has been reported.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: INC and The Gentlemen ransomware affiliates ran AI-agent intrusions against edge devices, exposed server shows
item.description:
SOCRadar found an exposed server belonging to a Russian-speaking operator serving INC and The Gentlemen ransomware affiliates, running an AI framework called Phantom that executed intrusions through OpenCode and commercial models while a human approved each step. Logs covered 8,257 messages across 133 sessions. Initial access came from exploiting edge and remote-access systems at scale, including SimpleHelp CVE-2024-57727, FortiClient EMS CVE-2026-35616 and cPanel/WHM CVE-2026-41940, followed by credential theft, lateral movement and ransomware staging.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: CISA adds exploited Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw CVE-2026-114625 to KEV with a three-day deadline
item.description:
CISA added Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator SQL injection flaw CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS 9.9) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 23, with an unusually short federal deadline of October 26 and forensic triage required. Any authenticated VCO user, even with the lowest tenant role, can gain superuser operator privileges on on-prem deployments, which Arista says are exposed by default.

It is the third exploited VCO zero-day in four months. Fixed releases are 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12; Arista also lists two attacker IPs to block and hunt for in logs.

Sources: SecurityWeek, CISA KEV catalog, Arista advisory

item.title: k0t campaign breached FortiGate and GlobalProtect edge devices worldwide, exposing 70,000+ credentials
item.description:
Group-IB and NyxLab detailed a large campaign by an initial access broker tracked as k0t that indiscriminately hit exposed Fortinet FortiGate and Palo Alto GlobalProtect devices, exposing more than 70,000 credentials. Most compromises happened between February and June 2026, overlapping the FortiBleed credential-harvesting wave, and some victims saw persistent access and data theft. The actor is linked to the Qilin and The Gentlemen ransomware operations.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Huntress: token-spraying campaign hijacked Microsoft 365 mailboxes at 79 organizations without passwords
item.description:
Huntress tracked an attacker who, from July 14 to September 22, replayed stolen Microsoft 365 session tokens (gathered via adversary-in-the-middle phishing and device-code phishing) to break into email accounts at 79 organizations, bypassing MFA. The attacker registered at least 48 rogue devices in victims' Entra directories and used hidden inbox rules to hide mail from victims. Sign-ins came from a handful of addresses in 193.26.115.0/24 hosted by 1337 Services GmbH.

Source: Help Net Security

item.title: Critical Pillow flaw CVE-2026-112900 allows command execution via a crafted EPS filename; fixed in 13.0.0
item.description:
Pillow, Python's most widely used image library (about 436 million downloads a month), passes EPS filenames to Ghostscript unchecked, so an attacker who controls the filename can get OS commands run on hosts with Ghostscript installed. The bug, CVE-2026-112900 (rated 9.2 in the GitHub CVE record), affects versions 2.6.0 through 12.3.0 and is fixed in Pillow 13.0.0, a large security release. No exploitation is known.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Imperva's Node2Shell demo turns Node.js Brotli bug CVE-2026-111497 into code execution on an official build
item.description:
Imperva showed crafted Brotli data running attacker code on the official Node.js 24.22.0 Linux arm64 build via the bundled Brotli decoder (CVE-2026-111497), going beyond the earlier crash-only proof of concept. The flaw affects the 22.x, 24.x and 26.x lines and is reachable through built-in fetch() responses or Express 5 body parsers decoding Brotli request bodies. Node.js shipped fixes on October 21 (24.22.1 rejects the data), and no in-the-wild exploitation has been reported.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: BIND 9 flaw CVE-2026-94300 lets replayed GSS-TSIG messages corrupt memory, possible RCE
item.description:
ISC disclosed a high-severity BIND 9 bug (CVSS 8.1) where replaying captured GSS-TSIG signed UDP messages, combined with crafted queries to an attacker-controlled zone, can corrupt memory in named and potentially lead to remote code execution. It affects BIND 9.11.0 through 9.18.50, 9.20.0 through 9.20.29, and 9.21.0 through 9.21.26; fixes are in 9.20.30 and 9.21.27, with no workaround.

ISC says it is not aware of active exploitation, and the risk is mainly for servers using GSS-TSIG with Kerberos. Dave Aitel of OpenAI independently reported it.

Source: ISC security advisory

item.title: Capcom confirms CAPCOM ID breach exposing 11.7 million accounts
item.description:
Capcom confirmed hackers breached its CAPCOM ID membership service, exposing more than 11.7 million customer email addresses along with account creation dates, login counts and last-login IP addresses. A small subset of 43 accounts also had birth dates, gender, nicknames and countries exposed, and attackers changed passwords on 196 accounts before Capcom reset them. Capcom says other passwords and credit card data were not exposed; it detected the intrusion on October 19.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Two CVSS 9.0 Linux KSMBD RCE flaws disclosed before kernel fixes, one pre-auth
item.description:
Trend Micro's ZDI publicly reported two remote code execution flaws in KSMBD, the Linux kernel's built-in SMB server, with no fix yet in mainline or linux-next and no CVEs assigned. ZDI-CAN-33774 is a handler-table race reachable before authentication on port 445, while ZDI-CAN-33549 is an integer underflow that needs SMB Direct over an RDMA-capable interface. KSMBD isn't enabled on many distros by default (RHEL doesn't ship it), so exposure is limited to systems running the module; admins can check with lsmod and block port 445 until patches land. No exploitation has been reported.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS business after eight intermediate CA keys were exposed
item.description:
Indian certificate authority eMudhra's board voted to withdraw from the global SSL/TLS certificate business, five days after a researcher recovered the private keys of eight of its intermediate CAs. Chrome will stop trusting the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 around the morning of October 27 PT, following Mozilla's Firefox decision on October 20. About 30,800 unexpired certificates chain to that root, 99.9% issued through Internet2's InCommon service for higher education, and Google says those site operators must replace them immediately. eMudhra says it will swap affected customers to free certificates from unnamed partners.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Arista patches VeloCloud Orchestrator zero-day exploited in attacks (CVE-2026-114625)
item.description:
Arista released fixes for CVE-2026-114625, a critical SQL injection flaw in on-prem VeloCloud Orchestrator, the SD-WAN management portal, that is being exploited in attacks. It needs a valid authenticated session but lets any user escalate to a "superuser operator" and reach internal-only functions on the VCO host. Arista says hosted VCO is already patched and urges on-prem admins to update, restrict the web interface to admin networks, and block two attacker IPs. It's Arista's fourth exploited zero-day this year.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Amazon: PHP2Shell exploit attempts started four days before patches shipped
item.description:
Amazon Threat Intelligence says it caught an attempt to exploit the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) against its MadPot honeypots on October 17, four days before PHP shipped patches on October 21 and while the bugs were still under embargo. The attempt came from an anonymization-network IP, and it is unclear how the attacker got exploit details early. Several security firms have since reported further exploit attempts after the patches came out, so unpatched PHP 7.x and 8.x servers should be treated as at risk.

Sources: BleepingComputer, The Hacker News

item.title: Microsoft ties ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply chain attack to China-linked Storm-0940 using ARTEX AI agents
item.description:
Microsoft says the China state-aligned actor Storm-0940 was behind the recent compromise of the ConnectWise Cloud Backup app. The group used ARTEX, an agentic AI penetration-testing framework, to automate reconnaissance, password spraying and abuse of the already-consented OAuth app against hundreds of organizations since September 2026. Targets span defense, government, energy, finance, semiconductors, software and more, and the app access let the attackers authenticate without any interactive user sign-in.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: INTERPOL's Operation Serengeti III arrests 1,462 and disrupts 10,909 cybercrime networks in Africa
item.description:
INTERPOL says Operation Serengeti III, run from June 29 to August 31, 2026 across 21 countries, disrupted 10,909 malicious networks, arrested 1,462 suspects and recovered more than $105 million. Investigators identified 65,929 victims and linked the activity to losses above $385 million, with private partners such as Group-IB and Team Cymru supplying intelligence on phishing kits and botnets.

Sources: The Hacker News, BleepingComputer

item.title: Oracle's October 2026 Critical Patch Update fixes 1,209 CVEs, 95 of them critical
item.description:
Oracle's October 2026 CPU ships 1,295 patches for 1,209 unique CVEs, including 95 rated critical and 439 rated high, according to Tenable's analysis. Fusion Middleware got the most fixes (206), and 134 of those can be exploited remotely without authentication. E-Business Suite, Siebel CRM, PeopleSoft, JD Edwards, MySQL and Java SE also received large batches.

Source: SecurityWeek

item.title: QPACK flaws let one unauthenticated connection crash many HTTP/3 servers; three stacks still unpatched
item.description:
FoxIO found QPACK header-expansion bugs in seven of ten HTTP/3 stacks it tested, letting a remote unauthenticated attacker force up to 4,000-fold memory amplification and knock servers offline, and it released working proof-of-concept code. Fixes are out for quic-go (used by Caddy, Traefik and cloudflared), Cloudflare quiche, lsquic and Wireshark, while Bun, the h3 Rust library and aioquic were unpatched at disclosure. The impact is denial of service only, with no attacks seen in the wild.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: CBC: 1.5 million Canadian Crime Stoppers tips exposed in P3 Global Intel hack
item.description:
A CBC investigation found that more than 1.5 million tips submitted to Canadian Crime Stoppers programs over 25 years were exposed in the March 2026 hack of P3 Global Intel, the Navigate360-owned tip platform. About 850,000 records contain personal details such as addresses, phone numbers, emails, licence plates and some banking data tied to cash rewards, and CBC was able to contact more than a dozen tipsters from the data.

The data was stolen by the hacktivist group Internet Yiff Machine as part of a wider leak of more than 8 million P3 records shared with journalists through Distributed Denial of Secrets. Crime Stoppers has not yet detailed the breach scope.

Sources: CBC News, Reuters (March)

item.title: Railway breach exposes customer environment variables, deployments paused
item.description:
Cloud deployment platform Railway says an unauthorized party may have accessed encrypted customer environment variables and, for some, the decrypted contents, which can include API keys and database and registry credentials. Railway ties it to a series of attacks on platform companies aimed at AI inference providers, has paused all deployments, and tells every user to rotate all stored secrets and review logs. Customers are already reporting their keys being used by third parties.

Sources: Railway security disclosure, Railway status page

item.title: PingCAP TiDB Cloud breach: FulcrumSec leaks control-plane, billing and customer API-key data
item.description:
PingCAP confirmed that an attacker used stolen service-account credentials to access its internal cloud systems from September 9 to October 7, copying source code, account and billing records, SQL editor text, and encrypted TiDB Cloud API keys. Extortion group FulcrumSec claims 10.6 TB stolen, including 115K plaintext customer API keys and 180K tenant orgs, and has released 200 GB; PingCAP says it found no evidence customer databases were touched. TiDB Cloud customers should rotate API keys and review access logs.

Sources: Dark Reading, PingCAP incident report

item.title: Japan's Onamae Desktop Cloud hacked, malware on up to 27,000 customer servers
item.description:
Attackers breached the infrastructure of Onamae.com Desktop Cloud, a GMO Internet VPS service popular in Japan for automated FX trading, and installed malware on up to 26,739 customer servers. GMO began shutting down all Desktop Cloud servers at 4 AM local time on October 21 with no restart date, and warns that data on affected servers may be exposed. Customers who stored passwords or other secrets on those servers should rotate them now.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Lazarus uses post-quantum cryptography to deliver malware in FlashHole campaign
item.description:
Kaspersky says North Korea's Lazarus Group is running a campaign it calls FlashHole against South Korean organizations, using the post-quantum ML-KEM-1024 key exchange to protect malware delivery from its command servers. The chain starts with phishing pages pointing to crafted GitHub pages, abuses the INISAFE CrossWeb EX security tool and the Windows fsquirt.exe binary to run shellcode, and pulls more malware from private GitHub repositories. The activity dates back to July 2025.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Critical GitLab flaw (CVSS 10.0) allows unauthenticated RCE on self-managed servers back to 7.0
item.description:
GitLab patched CVE-2026-110264 on October 21, a CVSS 10.0 integer overflow in the bundled Onigmo regex engine that can let an unauthenticated attacker run code on self-managed GitLab servers. Every version back to 7.0 (2014) is affected, and fixes were backported to 18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9 and 19.2.9 alongside 19.3.6, 19.4.3 and 19.5.1. Instances patched on October 12 are in range again. GitLab reports no exploitation so far and it is not in CISA KEV; GitLab.com and Dedicated are already fixed.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Ransomware gangs have been exploiting Palo Alto GlobalProtect auth bypass CVE-2026-0257 since June
item.description:
Several ransomware groups are exploiting CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass in the PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal and gateway (and Prisma Access) that lets remote, unauthenticated attackers set up an unauthorized VPN connection. Palo Alto patched it in May and first rated it medium severity, but victims now span healthcare, education, government and energy. Unpatched GlobalProtect devices should be updated and checked for unexpected VPN sessions.

Source: Help Net Security

item.title: OVHcloud CLI releases v0.11.0 through v0.15.0 on GitHub were tampered with to steal secrets
item.description:
An attacker used a developer's GitHub account to add an info-stealing binary to OVHcloud's open-source command-line tool, affecting versions v0.11.0 through v0.15.0. The tampered releases were live for about 90 minutes on October 19 before a customer reported them. OVHcloud says v0.16.0 is clean and anyone who downloaded an affected release should update or delete it and rotate secrets on that machine.

Source: Help Net Security

item.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI and Docker shipped a credential stealer and hourly remote code loader
item.description:
All seven wheels of the popular AI gateway library LiteLLM 1.107.0, published to PyPI on October 21, contained malware that runs on every Python start via cook.pth and sitecustomize.py, stealing cloud, SSH, Kubernetes, CI and AI-tool secrets and installing an hourly remote code loader. Docker images tagged v1.107.0, latest, main-latest and main-stable were also affected. PyPI pulled the release; anyone who installed it should treat the host as compromised, rotate every reachable credential and pin to 1.106.2.

Sources: StepSecurity, AISLE, Cyber Security News

item.title: CyberCartel used a multi-model AI agent system to attack 400+ Latin American banks, Straiker reports
item.description:
Straiker documented CARLIY0S, a multi-agent attack system built on the PentAGI framework that the long-running CyberCartel group used against more than 400 Latin American banks and payment providers. It assigned Claude, Grok and Kimi models to reconnaissance, exploit development and target decisions, and Straiker found a stolen-credential database of 4,493 records. It is one of the first detailed looks at criminals running AI-orchestrated intrusions at scale.

Sources: Straiker, Benzinga

item.title: PHP2Shell patches released for critical PHP RCE flaws; exploitation attempts reported in the wild
item.description:
PHP shipped emergency fixes (8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35) for the PHP2Shell runtime flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which allow unauthenticated RCE on nearly every PHP version back to 5.4. Cloudflare and watchTowr see exploitation attempts in the wild, and governments worldwide issued urgent warnings. This is a material update to yesterday's pre-patch item and is also posted to the breaking feed.

Sources: The Record, The Hacker News, Help Net Security

item.title: Attackers hijacked 300+ Tor exit relays to intercept SSH logins
item.description:
Attackers compromised the Linux hosts behind more than 300 Tor exit relays in early October and rewrote their exit policies to redirect SSH traffic to 12 interception servers that harvested passwords. At the Oct 4 peak the relays carried about 7.5% of Tor's exit capacity; the Tor Project had removed them all by Oct 5. Anyone who logged into SSH with a password over Tor between Oct 1 and 5 and accepted a new host key should rotate that password.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Stolen UpdraftCentral connection keys used to backdoor WordPress sites after TeamUpdraft breach; up to ~400K sites exposed
item.description:
TeamUpdraft, maker of UpdraftPlus, says attackers breached teamupdraft.com over the weekend of October 17-18 and likely accessed its customer database, including password hashes, 2FA settings and UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault and UpdraftClone connection keys. Patchstack says attackers began using the stolen keys on October 18 to push at least 99 disguised backdoor plugins and add admin accounts on connected sites, and estimates around 400,000 sites have an UpdraftCentral or Migrator key. Nethemba confirmed malicious plugins on two of its own fully patched sites.

Update UpdraftPlus to 1.26.13 (free) or 2.26.13 (Premium) or later, delete existing UpdraftCentral keys on each site, check for indicators of compromise, and restore from clean backups if compromised.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: PHP readies emergency patches for two leaked critical RCE flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) affecting PHP 5 through 8
item.description:
The PHP security team says it will ship emergency updates on Wednesday, October 21 at 7:00 AM PT for two critical vulnerabilities rated 9.2 under CVSS v4.0, after details leaked ahead of the planned embargo. watchTowr says both are remote code execution bugs believed to affect PHP 5, 6, 7 and 8, and that it has reproduced one of them. No exploitation in the wild has been observed yet, and PHP says it may release earlier if details go public or attacks start.

Admins running PHP should be ready to patch as soon as the fixed releases land.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Zeabur shutting down after second breach: leaked plaintext admin credentials exposed 3.2M environment-variable records and 321,810 accounts
item.description:
Developer hosting platform Zeabur is shutting down after its second breach in two months. On October 14-15 an attacker used leaked internal credentials, stored in plaintext and never rotated after the August breach, to get into shared clusters in nine regions, dedicated servers and the production database, stealing about 3.2 million environment-variable records and data on 321,810 accounts. Zeabur also confirmed root sign-ins on 101 GCP servers, SSH keys added to 50 servers, and 16 customer disk copies attached to attacker machines.

Anyone who deployed on Zeabur should rotate every secret, API key and database credential that was stored in its environment variables.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: CISA adds the Plex2Shell chain (four Plex Media Server CVEs) to KEV, confirming exploitation
item.description:
CISA added CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655 and CVE-2026-96656 in Plex Media Server to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 20 (catalog version 2026.10.20). These are the four bugs in the Plex2Shell chain, which lets an attacker go from SSRF with any X-Plex-Token to writing files that run on load. This is an update to the October 18 item, where exploitation had only been reported from a honeypot.

Plex shipped fixes in August; anyone running Plex Media Server older than 1.43.3.10861, especially exposed to the internet, should update now. CISA also added an exploited SiteGuard Server Edition command-injection bug (CVE-2026-106931, covered earlier) and a local Siemens Software Center DLL-loading flaw (CVE-2026-110936) the same day.

Source: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog

item.title: Mozilla and Chrome confirm private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CAs were compromised; trust stores rush fixes
item.description:
Mozilla and the Chrome Root Program confirmed on October 20 that the private keys of eight eMudhra (emSign) intermediate CAs, six for TLS and two for code signing, are compromised. Anyone holding them could issue certificates any site would trust. A researcher reported it on October 17, and Chrome and Firefox blocked the keys within hours. No certificates from them had appeared in Certificate Transparency logs before the block, and it is still unknown how the keys left eMudhra or who else holds them.

Mozilla has removed the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from NSS, and Chrome plans to drop it too. Apple and Microsoft have blocked the certificates, and fixes shipped in Go 1.27.3/1.26.10, Firefox 158.0.1, Python certifi and Rust webpki-roots, while Node.js is still pending. Software that doesn't check revocation needs updating or rebuilding. This confirms the CA behind the urgent Go release reported earlier today.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Public exploit released for critical unauthenticated FortiSIEM RCE (CVE-2026-106173)
item.description:
Horizon3.ai published a proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-106173 (CVSS 9.4), the FortiSIEM path traversal Fortinet patched last week. An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the gRPC service on TCP port 27918 can combine "../" sequences with a null byte to overwrite a Redis health-check script that cron runs every 60 seconds, turning a file write into code execution.

FortiSIEM 7.5.0 is affected (fixed in 7.5.1 and later) and 7.6 is not. No exploitation has been reported yet, but with a public exploit out, unpatched exposed instances are now at high risk. Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Qilin and INC ransomware gangs exploit PAN-OS GlobalProtect auth bypass (CVE-2026-0257), then pivot to vCenter and ESXi
item.description:
Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 says ransomware crews Qilin (Spikey Scorpius) and INC (Tarnished Scorpius) are still exploiting CVE-2026-0257, a PAN-OS and Prisma Access authentication bypass patched in May and in CISA's KEV catalog since May 13. They use it to set up VPN sessions that skip MFA, then move laterally over RDP and SMB.

In one case the attackers went from the VPN gateway to vCenter, disabled ESXi protections and dumped domain credentials straight from a domain controller's virtual disk, getting around in-guest EDR. Palo Alto urges patching plus a hunt for suspicious gateway-connected events. Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Paradigm Healthcare breach exposed data on 970,000 Medi-Cal members, notified 11 months after intrusion
item.description:
Paradigm Healthcare Services, which handles billing for California's Medi-Cal program, told HHS that an intrusion detected in October 2025 affected more than 970,000 people. Files accessed between Oct 8 and Oct 15, 2025 held names, dates of birth, gender and Medi-Cal member ID numbers.

Notification letters went out Sept 14, 2026, about 11 months after detection. No group has claimed the attack, and Paradigm hasn't said how attackers got in or whether data was exfiltrated. Source: SecurityWeek

item.title: OVHcloud CLI releases v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 backdoored on GitHub to steal developer secrets
item.description:
An attacker hijacked a developer's GitHub account and swapped in info-stealing builds for OVHcloud CLI versions 0.11.0 through 0.15.0, which were live from 14:47 to 16:21 (Paris time) on October 19 before a customer reported them. The malware's goal was to pull secrets off disk. CEO Octave Klaba said release immutability was turned off, so existing releases could be modified without going through CI. Versions 0.10.0 and 0.16.0 are clean, and anyone who installed a bad build should remove it and rotate credentials.

Sources: BleepingComputer, The Hacker News

item.title: Go ships urgent 1.27.3 and 1.26.10 releases that block eight CA intermediate keys, reportedly eMudhra's
item.description:
Go 1.27.3 and 1.26.10, shipped on its URGENT security track on October 20, make Go's certificate verifier reject any chain that passes through eight intermediate CA keys, citing "specific security concerns around their operation." The Go team did not name the CA, but a commenter matched the key hashes to eMudhra emSign intermediates, and Mozilla added six emSign intermediates to its OneCRL blocklist on October 17 through a non-public bug. Go recommends upgrading immediately, and services chained to those keys will fail with an x509 error.

Source: The Hacker News
